title: Ingress Controllers 🕹️
description: Install and understand the engine that powers Ingress – the controller.

slides.title: No Built‑in Controller 🚫
slides.content:
# Kubernetes doesn’t come with one

Unlike other objects, an Ingress resource alone does nothing. You must deploy an **Ingress controller** to the cluster. It watches the API for Ingress objects and updates the underlying load balancer.

Popular controllers:
- **ingress‑nginx** (Kubernetes community)
- **Traefik**
- **HAProxy**
- **AWS Load Balancer Controller** (for ALB)
- **Contour** (Envoy‑based)

slides.title: Installing ingress‑nginx (minikube) 🛠️
slides.content:
## Simplest for local dev

Minikube bundles the NGINX Ingress controller as an addon:
```bash
minikube addons enable ingress
```

For other clusters, use the official manifest:
```bash
kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/main/deploy/static/provider/cloud/deploy.yaml
```

This creates a `ingress-nginx` namespace with the controller Deployment and Service of type LoadBalancer.

quizData.question: True or False: An Ingress resource will route traffic even if no Ingress controller is installed.
quizData.explanation: The controller is needed to actually implement the routing rules.

slides.title: How Controllers Work 🔄
slides.content:
## The reconciliation loop

1. Controller watches for new/changed Ingress objects.
2. It reads the rules and builds a configuration for its proxy (e.g., nginx.conf).
3. When a Service or Endpoints change, it updates the configuration.
4. It also manages TLS certificates if you reference a Secret in the Ingress.

This happens automatically – no manual reloads needed.

slides.title: Verify Controller Deployment
slides.content: After enabling the minikube ingress addon:
slides.codeSnippet:
kubectl get pods -n ingress-nginx
kubectl get svc -n ingress-nginx

slides.title: Ingress Class 🏷️
slides.content:
## Multiple controllers in one cluster

If you install several controllers, you need to tell each Ingress resource which controller to use. Use the `ingressClassName` field:

```yaml
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
```

The class must match a `IngressClass` resource defined by the controller.

From Kubernetes 1.18+, this is the standard way (not the old annotation).

quizData.question: Why would you use `ingressClassName`?

options.text: To select which Ingress controller handles this Ingress

quizData.explanation: It ensures the correct controller processes the Ingress when multiple exist.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use the NGINX Ingress controller for most cases

It’s mature, widely used, and well‑documented. For cloud‑native L7 load balancers (like AWS ALB), use the cloud‑specific controller.
